question.question:
A plant is built in two stages: capex of USD 8500 at time zero and USD 6000 at the beginning of year 2. The beginning of year t is the same instant as the end of year t-1; time zero is the beginning of year 1. Operating inflows arrive at each year-end for 4 years: USD 3500 in year 1, then changing -7.5 percent per year (negative means decline). Working capital must equal 15 percent of the coming year's inflow, set at the beginning of that year; each adjustment is the change from the prior balance (zero before year 1), an increase being an outflow and a decrease a release at that instant. At the end of year 4, 60 percent of the final balance is recovered and the rest is lost. The annual discount rate is 8 percent. Compute the project NPV at time zero.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Present value of both capex stages combined.
Total present value of all end-of-year operating inflows.
Net present value of beginning-of-year working-capital adjustments, positive meaning net outflow.
Present value of the recovered working capital at project end.
